headline: NVIDIA Opens Vera Rubin Architecture to Data Centers
dek: The company hands its rack designs to the Open Compute Project and publishes open standards, per its own announcement.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: Rack designs opened to the industry
body: NVIDIA opened the hardware specifications of its Vera Rubin architecture at the OCP Global Summit in the United States (NVIDIA).
According to the company, the rack and tray designs go to the Open Compute Project through the open MGX architecture.

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: What MGX 1.2 brings
s3.body: According to NVIDIA, the new version of the specification includes:

points.t: Blind-mate liquid cooling, no hoses connected by hand (NVIDIA).
19-inch racks and deployments up to 250 kW (NVIDIA).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: A rack for AI agents
body: NVIDIA also introduced the Vera CPU rack, built for AI agents, with tool calling and sandboxed execution.
According to the company, it sits alongside the Vera Rubin NVL72, its base for large-scale training and inference.

stat.cap: per rack, supported by MGX 1.2, NVIDIA says

items.t: With AMD, Google and Meta, NVIDIA published version 0.7 of an open specification.
With Google, Meta and Microsoft, it set how infrastructure reacts to grid faults (NVIDIA).
NVIDIA gave no pricing; the specifications are open, the company says.

caption.hook: NVIDIA opened its Vera Rubin architecture to the industry, handing the rack designs to the Open Compute Project.
body: According to NVIDIA, the MGX 1.2 specification adds blind-mate liquid cooling, a 5,000-amp power busbar and support for deployments up to 250 kW per rack.

The company also introduced the Vera CPU rack, built for AI agents, and says it published open standards with AMD, Google, Meta and Microsoft for data centers and power grid resilience. The information comes from NVIDIA's own announcement, and the company gave no pricing.
caption.cta: Should AI hardware standards be open to everyone?
